claims.claim_text: Wallach holds that taking vitamins and minerals only at Recommended Daily Allowance (RDA) levels is better than nothing but will not prevent serious degenerative diseases — among them arthritis, osteoporosis, arteriosclerosis, senile dementia, muscular dystrophy, cystic fibrosis, pyorrhea (gum disease), heart attack and cancer.
claims.verbatim:
Food supplements at RDA
levels are better than nothing but will not
prevent serious disease (i.e., arthritis,
osteoporosis, arteriosclerosis, senile dementia,
muscular dystrophy, cystic fibrosis, pyorrhea,
heart attack, cancer, etc.).

claims.claim_text: Wallach distinguishes "preventive doses" of vitamins and minerals — fairly well established, and considerably higher than the Recommended Daily Allowance (RDA) but below the "megavitamin" range — from megavitamin levels, which he reserves for extraordinary situations and specific diseases.
claims.verbatim:
"Preventive doses" of vitamin
andminerals are fairly well established (Table
8-1). These are considerably higher than
RDAs but not in the "megavitamin" range.

fatigue

insomnia

pale smooth tongue
